# select_default_role (Resource)

One role that every member of the organization holds by default, on the whole organization or on one resource. Use one of these per grant.

## About

Each `select_default_role` grants one role to every member of the organization, on one scope. Default grants that Terraform does not manage are not changed. An organization can have no default grants.

Omit `scope` to grant the role on the whole organization. To grant it on one resource, set `scope.type` and `scope.id`.

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/default-roles`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every member of the organization can view everything.
resource "select_default_role" "everyone_views" {
  role = "viewer"
}

# Every member of the organization can create teams.
resource "select_default_role" "everyone_creates_teams" {
  role = "team_creator"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `role` (String) The role every organization member holds: `admin`, `editor`, `monitor_editor`, `viewer` or `team_creator`. Changing it forces a new grant.

### Optional

- `scope` (Attributes) The resource the role applies to. Omit it to grant the role on the whole organization. `id` is required for every `type` except `organization`. Changing it forces a new grant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the grant was created — RFC 3339 UTC, e.g. 2026-06-05T10:30:00Z.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this grant. Sent as `If-Match` on deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The grant's identifier in SELECT, assigned when the role is granted. Use it with `terraform import` to bring an existing grant under management.
- `update_time` (String) When the grant was last updated — RFC 3339 UTC.

<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Required:

- `type` (String) The kind of resource the grant applies to: `organization`, `snowflake_organization`, `snowflake_account`, `databricks_account`, `databricks_connection`, `bigquery_connection`, `aws_account`, `tableau_site` or `usage_group`.

Optional:

- `id` (String) The resource's identifier: the Snowflake organization name, the Snowflake account UUID, the Databricks account id, or the id SELECT gave the Databricks connection, BigQuery connection, AWS account, Tableau site (its LUID) or usage group. Leave it unset for `organization`.

## Import

`select_default_role` can be imported using the grant's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_default_role.example <role_id>
```

To find the ID, list the default role grants with the API:

```bash
curl -s https://api.select.dev/v2/default-roles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SELECT_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: $SELECT_ORGANIZATION_ID" | jq '.items[] | {id, role, entity}'
```

## Additional Information

### Every change replaces the grant

The API cannot change a default role grant. A change to `role` or `scope` revokes the grant and makes a new one. Every member of the organization loses the role for a short time between the two.

### How the provider reads a grant

The API has no route that returns one default role grant, so the provider lists the default grants and finds this one by its ID. If the grant is not in the list, for example because someone revoked it in the SELECT UI, the next plan grants it again.

### A grant that already exists

If SELECT refuses the grant with a conflict, the same default role can already exist on the same scope. Import that grant instead of creating it again.

### Changes made outside Terraform

A delete carries the grant's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so it is refused if the grant changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.
